assumptions: K is real and continuous on R
K[t] is the compact self-adjoint Suzuki truncation

exact.conditional_inner_result: If E_(omega,nu) belongs to HB, Suzuki Proposition 5.1 gives a full L2 isometry K, K[t]=P_t K P_t, and ||K[t]||<1 for every finite t
exact.determinant_contractivity: For every T>=0: det(I+/-K[t])!=0 for all 0<=t<=T iff ||K[T]||<1 iff ||K[t]||<1 for all 0<=t<=T
exact.effective_interval: K[t] vanishes on inputs supported in (-infinity,-t) and its output vanishes on (-infinity,-t); it is therefore represented by the continuous kernel K(x+y) on the finite square (-t,t)^2
exact.first_crossing: If T_*=inf{t>=0: ||K[t]||=1}<infinity, compact self-adjointness forces +1 or -1 to be an eigenvalue of K[T_*], so det(I-K[T_*])=0 or det(I+K[T_*])=0
exact.fixed_space: For (U_t f)(u)=f(t-u), u>0: A_t=U_t K[t] U_t^(-1), (A_t g)(u)=integral_0^infinity K(2t-u-v)g(v)dv
exact.high_contour_ceiling: T_HC(omega,nu)=sup_(v>1/2+omega) [log(1/M_v)]_+/(2v)<infinity; the certificate M_v^2*exp(4v*t)<1 cannot prove any t>T_HC
exact.high_contour_certificate: Suzuki's Proposition 4.2 eigenfunction contradiction is certified when M_v^2*exp(4v*t)<1 for some v>1/2+omega, where M_v=sup_(u in R)|Theta_(omega,nu)(u+i*v)|
exact.hilbert_schmidt_growth: If c_R=integral_0^R |K(s)|^2 ds>0, then for t>R/2: ||K[t]||_HS^2 >= (2t-R)*c_R -> infinity
exact.isolated_time_guard: At one isolated time determinant nonvanishing is weaker: A=2P for a rank-one orthogonal projection has ||A||=2, det(I-A)=-1, and det(I+A)=3
exact.no_uniform_gap: Under the same HB hypothesis, P_t->I strongly and K is an isometry, so lim_(t->infinity)||K[t]||=1; no epsilon>0 can satisfy ||K[t]||<=1-epsilon for every t
exact.norm_monotonicity: For 0<=t_1<=t_2, ||K[t_1]||<=||K[t_2]||, because K[t_1] is the quadratic-form compression of the self-adjoint K[t_2]
exact.path_continuity: For continuous K with K(s)=0 on s<0, t -> A_t is continuous in Hilbert-Schmidt norm and A_0=0
exact.quadratic_form_target: The noncircular live target is, for every finite t and every nonzero f: |<K[t]f,f>|<||f||^2, equivalently I+K[t]>0 and I-K[t]>0
exact.terminal_sequence_reduction: For one fixed pair, pointwise-in-t strict contractivity does not directly prove J(t;z,z)->0. On a strictly decreasing cofinal omega_n->0 sequence, however, all-time contractivity gives a bounded causal multiplier, forces RH by shifted-zero accumulation, and then Suzuki's Theorem 2.3 supplies the terminal limit
exact.zeta_vertical_asymptotic: For zeta and a=nu*omega: Theta_(omega,nu)(i*v)=[xi(v+1/2-omega)/xi(v+1/2+omega)]^nu ~(2*pi/v)^a as v->infinity

proof_boundary: This artifact proves the fixed-space translation, exact Hilbert-Schmidt identity, path continuity and monotonicity, the all-history determinant/contractivity equivalence, the first-crossing alternative, and finite-ceiling guards for Hilbert-Schmidt and Suzuki sup-contour certificates. It records Suzuki's conditional HB contraction theorem and proves that its norms tend to one. Together with the separately checked causal-multiplier reduction, it records that the terminal premise is redundant for a cofinal determinant family. It does not prove the signed quadratic-form target, global Fredholm nonvanishing for zeta without HB, the Phi Pick sign, PF-infinity, RH, or Lambda<=0.

rows.claim: Every Suzuki truncation is unitarily equivalent to a finite-triangle Hankel operator on one fixed half-line space.
rows.formula: For (U_t f)(u)=f(t-u), u>0: A_t=U_t K[t] U_t^(-1), (A_t g)(u)=integral_0^infinity K(2t-u-v)g(v)dv
rows.proof_boundary: This uses only the support K(s)=0 for s<0.

rows.claim: Although written on a half-line, the truncation acts only on a finite interval.
rows.formula: K[t] vanishes on inputs supported in (-infinity,-t) and its output vanishes on (-infinity,-t); it is therefore represented by the continuous kernel K(x+y) on the finite square (-t,t)^2
rows.proof_boundary: This does not bound its operator norm.

rows.claim: The Hilbert-Schmidt norm has a one-dimensional weighted-kernel formula.
rows.proof_boundary: The identity is valid for every locally square-integrable supported kernel.

rows.claim: For every nonzero continuous supported kernel, the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the truncations diverges.
rows.formula: If c_R=integral_0^R |K(s)|^2 ds>0, then for t>R/2: ||K[t]||_HS^2 >= (2t-R)*c_R -> infinity
rows.proof_boundary: This does not imply that the operator norm exceeds one.

rows.claim: The sufficient estimate ||K[t]||<=||K[t]||_HS<1 can only certify a bounded initial t-range.
rows.formula: If c_R=integral_0^R |K(s)|^2 ds>0, then for t>R/2: ||K[t]||_HS^2 >= (2t-R)*c_R -> infinity

rows.claim: The translated compact operators form a Hilbert-Schmidt-continuous path starting at zero.
rows.formula: For continuous K with K(s)=0 on s<0, t -> A_t is continuous in Hilbert-Schmidt norm and A_0=0
rows.proof_boundary: Suzuki Proposition 4.1 supplies continuity of the arithmetic kernel when nu*omega>1.

rows.claim: The truncation operator norm is nondecreasing in t.
rows.formula: For 0<=t_1<=t_2, ||K[t_1]||<=||K[t_2]||, because K[t_1] is the quadratic-form compression of the self-adjoint K[t_2]
rows.proof_boundary: Monotonicity alone does not keep the norm below one.

rows.claim: Along the whole connected truncation path, Suzuki's two determinant exclusions are exactly pointwise strict contractivity.
rows.formula: For every T>=0: det(I+/-K[t])!=0 for all 0<=t<=T iff ||K[T]||<1 iff ||K[t]||<1 for all 0<=t<=T

rows.claim: Any finite failure has a first spectral collision at +1 or -1.
rows.formula: If T_*=inf{t>=0: ||K[t]||=1}<infinity, compact self-adjointness forces +1 or -1 to be an eigenvalue of K[T_*], so det(I-K[T_*])=0 or det(I+K[T_*])=0
rows.proof_boundary: The open task is to rule out this first collision for the arithmetic kernel.

rows.claim: At a single isolated t, nonzero determinants do not imply contraction.
rows.formula: At one isolated time determinant nonvanishing is weaker: A=2P for a rank-one orthogonal projection has ||A||=2, det(I-A)=-1, and det(I+A)=3
rows.proof_boundary: The example is a logical spectral guard, not a Suzuki truncation path.

rows.claim: Suzuki's unconditional local interval follows from a weighted high-contour eigenfunction contradiction.
rows.formula: Suzuki's Proposition 4.2 eigenfunction contradiction is certified when M_v^2*exp(4v*t)<1 for some v>1/2+omega, where M_v=sup_(u in R)|Theta_(omega,nu)(u+i*v)|
rows.proof_boundary: The condition is sufficient and local, not necessary.

rows.claim: For each fixed zeta pair (omega,nu), Suzuki's M_v certificate has a finite t ceiling.
rows.formula: T_HC(omega,nu)=sup_(v>1/2+omega) [log(1/M_v)]_+/(2v)<infinity; the certificate M_v^2*exp(4v*t)<1 cannot prove any t>T_HC
rows.proof_boundary: This rejects only this sup-norm contour certificate, not every possible contour argument.

rows.claim: Hermite-Biehler innerness supplies strict contraction at every finite t.
rows.formula: If E_(omega,nu) belongs to HB, Suzuki Proposition 5.1 gives a full L2 isometry K, K[t]=P_t K P_t, and ||K[t]||<1 for every finite t
rows.proof_boundary: Using this implication to establish the same HB property would be circular.

rows.claim: In the desired HB case the finite-t norms approach one, so a t-uniform positive gap is impossible.
rows.formula: Under the same HB hypothesis, P_t->I strongly and K is an isometry, so lim_(t->infinity)||K[t]||=1; no epsilon>0 can satisfy ||K[t]||<=1-epsilon for every t
rows.proof_boundary: The target is strictness at each finite t, not one epsilon valid for all t.

rows.claim: The surviving noncircular spectral task is a signed quadratic-form barrier against finite first crossing.
rows.formula: The noncircular live target is, for every finite t and every nonzero f: |<K[t]f,f>|<||f||^2, equivalently I+K[t]>0 and I-K[t]>0
rows.proof_boundary: No arithmetic factorization or coercive identity proving this is currently known in the corpus.

rows.claim: The terminal premise is fixed-family independent but cofinal-sequence redundant.
rows.formula: For one fixed pair, pointwise-in-t strict contractivity does not directly prove J(t;z,z)->0. On a strictly decreasing cofinal omega_n->0 sequence, however, all-time contractivity gives a bounded causal multiplier, forces RH by shifted-zero accumulation, and then Suzuki's Theorem 2.3 supplies the terminal limit
rows.proof_boundary: This uses the separately checked determinant-only causal-multiplier reduction and does not derive the terminal limit directly from one fixed family.

sources.title: Masatoshi Suzuki, Hamiltonians arising from L-functions in the Selberg class

status: exact truncation-path spectral reformulation, finite-ceiling route guards, one open signed quadratic-form target, and an internally audited cofinal terminal reduction
